keyEvents.event: Independence and the confessional National Pact
keyEvents.impact: Power divided by sect: a Maronite president, Sunni premier and Shia speaker, a formula that still governs
Fifteen years of sectarian war, Syrian and Israeli occupations and militia rule

keyEvents.event: Israeli invasion and siege of Beirut; birth of Hezbollah
keyEvents.impact: Iran's Revolutionary Guards founded the most powerful non-state army in the region

keyEvents.event: Taif Agreement ends the civil war
keyEvents.impact: Rebalanced sectarian power but left Hezbollah armed as the 'resistance'

keyEvents.event: Assassination of Rafik Hariri and the Cedar Revolution
keyEvents.impact: Syrian troops withdrew; politics split into pro- and anti-Hezbollah camps
Massive destruction; UN Resolution 1701 demanded Hezbollah disarm south of the Litani, never enforced

keyEvents.event: Financial collapse and the 2020 Beirut port explosion
keyEvents.impact: One of the worst economic crises in modern history wiped out savings and gutted the middle class

keyEvents.event: Israel decapitates Hezbollah, killing Hassan Nasrallah; November ceasefire
keyEvents.impact: Hezbollah's aura of invincibility broken and its Syrian supply line lost when Assad fell weeks later

keyEvents.event: Joseph Aoun elected president and Nawaf Salam named prime minister; cabinet mandates the army to disarm Hezbollah
keyEvents.impact: First government in decades openly committed to a state monopoly on arms

keyEvents.event: Hezbollah joins the Iran war; Israel invades and occupies southern Lebanon; elections postponed to 2028; June framework agreement with Israel
keyEvents.impact: Lebanon is again a battlefield, with disarmament now tied to Israeli withdrawal

history.narrative: A fragile confessional republic whose state has never held a monopoly on force, caught between an Iranian-built militia and an Israeli army that occupies its south. Bankrupt and war-scarred, it survives on diaspora remittances, Gulf and Western aid, and the hope that a reformist presidency can finally bring Hezbollah's guns under the state.

redLines.description: Permanent Israeli occupation or buffer zone in southern Lebanon
Collapse of the sectarian balance or a return to civil war
Cutoff of Gulf and Western aid and reconstruction funding

internalDivisions.name: Hezbollah and the Shia community versus Christian and Sunni parties over disarmament
Banking-crisis losers versus the entrenched political-financial elite
Over a million Syrian refugees and Palestinian camps

goals.description: Secure a full Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon and an end to strikes
Bring Hezbollah's arsenal under exclusive Lebanese Armed Forces control without civil war
Unlock Gulf and IMF money for reconstruction and banking-sector rescue
Demarcate and secure the Syrian border and return refugees
